notice: All manufacturers, models and liveries in this pack are original fiction. No real-world marks are used.

Ishara.ethos: Frugal, feather-light city cars with a cult tuning scene.

Katsuro.ethos: Mass-market saloons by day, all-wheel-drive giant killers by night.

Ryuzaki.ethos: Rotary obsessives. Light, revvy, and allergic to pistons.

Mishima.ethos: Heavy industry roots — indestructible trucks and one screaming halo car.

Hanyu.ethos: Value engineering that quietly grew a performance division.

Grauwolf.ethos: Precision executive machinery with a straight-six heartbeat.

Vorst.ethos: Rear-engine heresy, perfected over seventy years of flat sixes.

Eisenbach.ethos: Four-ring engineering: quattro traction and V10 theatrics.

Krallmann.ethos: A tuning house that outgrew its donors and started building its own.

Alviero.ethos: Front-engined V12 grand tourers with racing in the bloodline.

Valdoro.ethos: Angular V10 wedges built to intimidate first and corner second.

Wexler.ethos: Displacement is the answer. What was the question?

Marlowe.ethos: Pony cars, drag strips, and a stubborn love of pushrods.

Ironvale.ethos: Trucks and body-on-frame SUVs that treat kerbs as suggestions.

Apex Dynamics.ethos: Quad-motor electric hypercars from a company that was a battery startup.

Ashcombe.ethos: Hand-built luxury GTs with a V12 and a stiff upper lip.

Thornbury.ethos: Adds lightness. Removes carpet, radio, doors, and your fillings.

Aveline.ethos: Soft-riding oddballs that turn into rally monsters when provoked.

Norsken.ethos: Safe estates for the family, megacars for the other side of the garage.

cars.name: Ishara Kite
cars.blurb: The cheapest key in the garage. Nine hundred and fifty kilos of pure momentum management.

cars.name: Ishara Kite RS
cars.blurb: Stiffer springs, a red badge, and the first hint that Ishara has a sense of humour.

cars.name: Ishara Vela
cars.blurb: A rental-counter special that somehow became a drift-school favourite.

cars.name: Hanyu Pulse
cars.blurb: Ten-year warranty, zero pretension, surprising cornering manners.

cars.name: Hanyu Meridian
cars.blurb: Hanyu's midsize saloon. Comfortable, quiet, quietly quick.

cars.name: Hanyu Torro
cars.blurb: A crossover that thinks it's a hot hatch on stilts.

cars.name: Aveline Bonbon
cars.blurb: Three cylinders, four seats, and suspension tuned on cobblestones.

cars.name: Aveline Cirrus
cars.blurb: Soft, tall-riding, and startlingly composed once you commit to a corner.

cars.name: Aveline Marais
cars.blurb: The estate that hauls a family and, with the seats down, a spare engine.

cars.name: Katsuro Sable
cars.blurb: Katsuro's bread and butter. Ten million sold, one million modified.

cars.name: Katsuro Sable GT
cars.blurb: A factory-warm Sable with a small turbo and a big attitude.

cars.name: Katsuro Kaido
cars.blurb: Rear drive, skinny tyres, and a chassis that made a generation of mountain-pass legends.

cars.name: Katsuro Ronin 2.0
cars.blurb: Modern Kaido. Same recipe, better brakes, no rust.

cars.name: Ryuzaki Aki
cars.blurb: A folding roof, a slick gearbox, and nothing else to get in the way.

cars.name: Ryuzaki Kaze RX
cars.blurb: Two spinning triangles, nine thousand revs, and a thirst you learn to fund.

cars.name: Mishima Trail 4
cars.blurb: Mishima's workhorse. Torque like a tugboat, corners like a wardrobe.

cars.name: Mishima Ridgeback
cars.blurb: Seven seats, a locking diff, and no idea it's in a racing game.

cars.name: Grauwolf Kern 20
cars.blurb: Rear-drive executive basics. The cheapest way into the Grauwolf chassis.

cars.name: Grauwolf Kern 25 Touring
cars.blurb: The wagon that beat sports cars in the wet and carried the dog home after.

cars.name: Vorst Ceres
cars.blurb: Mid-engined, flat-four, and the purest steering rack under six figures.

cars.name: Wexler Coyote
cars.blurb: The V6 rental-spec Coyote. Everyone starts here. Nobody stays.

cars.name: Marlowe Comet
cars.blurb: Marlowe's entry pony car — all the shape, two thirds of the noise.

cars.name: Marlowe Dart 2.3T
cars.blurb: A four-cylinder pony car. Purists complained. It out-handled all of them.

cars.name: Ironvale Sentinel
cars.blurb: Body-on-frame, three tonnes of intent, physics be damned.

cars.name: Ironvale Mule 150
cars.blurb: A pickup in a racing game is a statement. Make it.

cars.name: Thornbury Wren
cars.blurb: Seven hundred and twenty kilograms. No carpet, no radio, no excuses.

cars.name: Norsken Frost 2.0T
cars.blurb: Safe, square, all-wheel drive. Deceptively fast on a wet road.

cars.name: Tenjin Ion
cars.blurb: Silent, instant off the line, and completely uninterested in gears.

cars.name: Tenjin Ion Dual
cars.blurb: Two motors, one pedal, and traction in places you didn't expect.

cars.name: Ashcombe Lyre
cars.blurb: Ashcombe's junior coupe. Leather, wood, and a surprisingly willing chassis.

cars.name: Katsuro Kaido Turbo
cars.blurb: A big single turbo bolted to a legend. Laggy, violent, adored.

cars.name: Katsuro Ronin RS
cars.blurb: The Ronin with the factory motorsport catalogue emptied into it.

cars.name: Katsuro Tessen GT
cars.blurb: Twin-turbo straight six, computer-controlled all-wheel drive, folk-hero status.

cars.name: Katsuro Tessen V-Spec
cars.blurb: Stiffer, wider, angrier. The one on everyone's bedroom wall.

cars.name: Katsuro Sable STX
cars.blurb: Homologation saloon. Gravel-bred, tarmac-capable, permanently sideways.

cars.name: Ryuzaki Kaze RX Turbo
cars.blurb: Boost meets rotary. The tachometer becomes a suggestion.

cars.name: Ryuzaki Shinkai FD
cars.blurb: Sequential twin turbos, a perfect silhouette, and a maintenance schedule from hell.

cars.name: Ryuzaki Aki S2
cars.blurb: Nine thousand revs from four cylinders. Torque is for other people.

cars.name: Ryuzaki Genbu Widebody
cars.blurb: A drift-spec Shinkai with fenders like shoulder pads and a hydraulic handbrake.

cars.name: Ishara Kite RS Cup
cars.blurb: Front-drive, limited-slip, and faster round a lap than cars costing four times more.

cars.name: Hanyu Meridian N
cars.blurb: Hanyu's skunkworks saloon. Pops, bangs, and a warranty that covers track days.

cars.name: Aveline Cirrus Rallye
cars.blurb: Aveline's rally homologation. Long-travel suspension and a co-driver seat.

cars.name: Vorst Ceres GTS
cars.blurb: They put the big flat six in the small car. Everything you hoped would happen, happened.

cars.name: Vorst Kessel S
cars.blurb: Engine still hanging out the back. Still shouldn't work. Still does.

cars.name: Vorst Kessel Turbo S
cars.blurb: All-wheel drive, two turbos, and launch control that rearranges your organs.

cars.name: Grauwolf Kern 40 CS
cars.blurb: Carbon roof, no rear seats, and a straight six tuned to sing at eight.

cars.name: Grauwolf Sturm 8
cars.blurb: A four-door with a twin-turbo V8 and absolutely no respect for its own tyres.

cars.name: Eisenbach Klasse 63
cars.blurb: Hand-built V8, quilted leather, and a drift mode nobody at head office admits to.

cars.name: Eisenbach Halde RS
cars.blurb: The fast estate. Groceries at nine tenths.

cars.name: Eisenbach Kreuz GT
cars.blurb: Naturally aspirated V10 in an aluminium spaceframe. The last of its kind.

cars.name: Wexler Coyote GT
cars.blurb: Five litres, a manual gearbox, and a soundtrack that sets off car alarms.

cars.name: Wexler Coyote Mach
cars.blurb: Supercharged, splitter'd, and wearing a wing you can see from orbit.

cars.name: Wexler Ironhide 440
cars.blurb: Big-block classic. Brakes are decorative. Straight lines only, mostly.

cars.name: Marlowe Comet SS
cars.blurb: The Comet with the proper engine. Balance sold separately.

cars.name: Marlowe Comet Venom
cars.blurb: Supercharged, widebodied, and quietly terrifying in the wet.

cars.name: Marlowe Dart Rally
cars.blurb: Marlowe's answer to the gravel crowd. Underdog energy.

cars.name: Thornbury Wren Cup
cars.blurb: Three hundred and fifty horsepower per tonne with a supercharger whine and no roof.

cars.name: Thornbury Harrier R
cars.blurb: Bonded aluminium tub, mid-mounted V6, and a steering rack wired to your spine.

cars.name: Norsken Frost R
cars.blurb: Electrified rear axle, snow tyres optional, dignity intact.

cars.name: Tenjin Ion GT
cars.blurb: Four hundred and eighty silent horsepower. The strangest thing you'll ever overtake with.

cars.name: Scorpetti Fiora
cars.blurb: Mid-engined, flat-plane, and calibrated to sound expensive at every rpm.

cars.name: Scorpetti Fiora Corsa
cars.blurb: Stripped, caged, and given a rear wing with an opinion.

cars.name: Scorpetti Tramonto
cars.blurb: Roof folds, noise doesn't. Scorpetti's open-top statement piece.

cars.name: Alviero Tempesta
cars.blurb: Front-mid V12, no turbos, no apologies. Eight thousand nine hundred revs.

cars.name: Alviero Aquilone
cars.blurb: The grand tourer. Cross a continent, then set a lap record on arrival.

cars.name: Alviero Nembo GTS
cars.blurb: The smaller Alviero. Twin turbos, shorter wheelbase, sharper temper.

cars.name: Valdoro Aventine
cars.blurb: Naturally aspirated V10, scissor doors, and a noise that sets off seismographs.

cars.name: Valdoro Aventine SV
cars.blurb: Lighter, louder, and wearing enough carbon to build a small aircraft.

cars.name: Valdoro Falco
cars.blurb: Rear-drive only, aero everywhere, built for people who've stopped pretending.

cars.name: Vorst Kessel RSR
cars.blurb: Naturally aspirated flat six at nine thousand. A homologation special for the road.

cars.name: Vorst Kessel Turbo GT
cars.blurb: The fastest thing Vorst will sell you with a number plate.

cars.name: Ashcombe Corvane
cars.blurb: Twelve cylinders wrapped in leather. Brutal, but politely.

cars.name: Ashcombe Thistle S
cars.blurb: The junior Ashcombe. Twin-turbo V8, tail-happy by design.

cars.name: Eisenbach Nordwand GT
cars.blurb: All-wheel drive, all-weather, all the time. The point-and-shoot supercar.

cars.name: Grauwolf Sturm 8 CSL
cars.blurb: Rear drive, no rear seats, and a Nürburgring time they won't stop mentioning.

cars.name: Katsuro Tessen Kaiju
cars.blurb: The Tessen reborn: hybrid-assisted V6, four driven wheels, zero nostalgia.

cars.name: Mishima Raiden V10
cars.blurb: Mishima's one and only halo car. Carbon tub, ten cylinders, a voice like a violin.

cars.name: Marlowe Comet ZX
cars.blurb: Marlowe finally put the engine behind the driver. It changed everything.

cars.name: Wexler Sidewinder V10
cars.blurb: Eight point four litres, no traction control worth the name, and a legend of a reputation.

cars.name: Thornbury Harrier GT1
cars.blurb: Six hundred and twenty horsepower per tonne. Thornbury's idea of restraint.

cars.name: Thornbury Lancet
cars.blurb: Hybrid-assisted, ground-effect, and legal on public roads by the narrowest margin.

cars.name: Ryuzaki Shinkai Type-R
cars.blurb: Four rotors. Nine thousand five hundred revs. A sound nothing else makes.

cars.name: Norsken Torden
cars.blurb: Sweden's first proper supercar. Twin turbos and a carbon monocoque.

cars.name: Tenjin Kaminari
cars.blurb: Three motors, torque vectoring, and total silence at two hundred.

cars.name: Apex Dynamics Surge
cars.blurb: Apex's entry point. Still quicker off the line than most things here.

cars.name: Alviero Divina
cars.blurb: Hybrid-assisted V12. Alviero's flagship, and the last naturally aspirated twelve they'll build.

cars.name: Scorpetti Aeterna
cars.blurb: Twin-turbo hybrid, active aero, and a price with too many digits.

cars.name: Valdoro Corvino
cars.blurb: A V12 hypercar shaped like a stealth fighter that lost an argument with a wind tunnel.

cars.name: Vorst Kaskade
cars.blurb: Le Mans technology, road-car warranty. Vorst's engineering flex.

cars.name: Grauwolf Projekt R
cars.blurb: A Formula One power unit with number plates. Idles like a machine gun.

cars.name: Krallmann Zorn 900
cars.blurb: Krallmann takes a V12, adds two turbos, and removes the concept of moderation.

cars.name: Krallmann Nachtfalter
cars.blurb: Matte black, rear drive, twelve hundred horsepower. Named after a moth. Behaves like a hornet.

cars.name: Norsken Ragnar
cars.blurb: Sixteen hundred horsepower in fourteen hundred kilos. The megacar arms race, won.

cars.name: Norsken Ragnar Absolut
cars.blurb: Long-tail bodywork built for one thing: the top-speed record.

cars.name: Ashcombe Solstice AM
cars.blurb: A thousand kilos, a screaming V12, and a cockpit you climb into feet first.

cars.name: Apex Dynamics Tempest EV
cars.blurb: Quad motors. Nineteen hundred horsepower. Silence, then the horizon.

cars.name: Apex Dynamics Halo X
cars.blurb: Apex's track-focused EV. Active aero, and brakes that recover more energy than most cars make.

cars.name: Mishima Raiden Omega
cars.blurb: The Raiden returns with hybrid assistance and a redline that never moved.

cars.name: Thornbury Vespera
cars.blurb: Thornbury's hypercar. They added lightness until there was almost nothing left.

cars.name: Wexler Thunderhead
cars.blurb: Sixteen cylinders, four turbos, and Detroit's answer to European excess.
